page.description: Shell on the aoox host or a remote server (<path></path>). Be careful: commands run directly on the target machine.

settingsPage.description: Where the web shell connects (local or SSH to the host) and the platform key it uses.

authorize.title: Authorize the terminal SSH key?
authorize.description: aoox will add the platform public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys of user {user} on this host. No password or private key is written.

card.sshDescription: Shell on the host over SSH to {target}
card.localDescription: Local shell next to the API process. In Docker, set TERMINAL_SSH_HOST so the terminal reaches the host.
card.authorizeInstruction: Run once on the host as user {user} so this key is allowed to log in:

view.ticketFailed: Could not create a terminal ticket.

origin.title: Terminal cannot be reached through this address
origin.description: This panel has a custom domain ({webOrigin}), and the Terminal only accepts connections from that domain, not from {browserOrigin} that you are using now. This is a built-in security protection, not a bug.

hint.title: The terminal could not connect to its target
hint.ownerOnly: Check its connection settings in <page></page>. Only the owner can open that page.
hint.checkSettings: Check its connection settings in <link></link>, then click Reconnect.
hint.sshAuthFailed: If the error is "SSH authentication failed": the authorization command must be run on the host as the same user as the User field in Environment. Root login is often refused by sshd on cloud VPS, so on Ubuntu set User to your login user (usually ubuntu), save, then run the authorization command as that user.
